poem.title: 鹿柴
poem.author: 王维
poem.text: 空山不见人，但闻人语响。返景入深林，复照青苔上。

user_prompt:
Translate this poem into literary English.
Title: 鹿柴
Author: 王维
Genre: 五言绝句
Source:
空山不见人，但闻人语响。返景入深林，复照青苔上。
translation:
**Deer Enclosure**

No one is seen on the empty mountain;  
only the sound of voices is heard.  
Returning sunlight enters the deep forest  
and shines once more upon the green moss.

message.reasoning_content:
I'll respond only English translation preserving title? User asks poem. I'll translate literary. Should decide title Deer Enclosure / Deer Park. Wang Wei "鹿柴" often "Deer Enclosure" or "Deer Park". Text:
空山不见人，但闻人语响。
返景入深林，复照青苔上。
Empty mountain, no one in sight, only hear echoes of voices. Returning sunlight enters deep forest, shines again on green moss.

Only English translation, preserving complete content poem structure. Could include title and author? User specifically title author genre source. Typically output title and poem, perhaps author not necessary? "Return only the English translation" likely title plus translated poem. Should have no explanations. Could render:
Deer Enclosure

No one is seen on the empty mountain;
only the sound of voices is heard.
Slanting sunlight enters the deep woods
and shines again upon the green moss.

"返景" reflected/returning sunlight, often "returning rays" or "slanting sunlight". Should have accurate relation: 返景入深林 "Returning sunlight enters the deep forest" and 复照青苔上 "shines once more on the green moss." 4 lines to match:
The mountain is empty; no one is seen,
Only the sound of voices is heard.
Returning sunlight enters the deep woods,
And shines again on the green moss.

Literary and natural. Title "Deer Enclosure" more literal 柴 zhai enclosure. Wang Wei poem standard title "Deer Enclosure". Could use "Deer Park" but that evokes Buddhist Deer Park, wrong perhaps. Deer Enclosure.

Should preserve 响 echo/resound. "but only hear voices echoing" implies speaker. "no one in sight; / only the echo of voices." Original "人语响" sound of human speech. I can do:
No one is seen in the empty mountains;
only the sound of voices is heard.
Returning sunlight enters the deep forest
and shines again upon the green moss.

Singular mountain original 空山. "The empty mountain shows no one;" weird. Best:
On the empty mountain, no one is seen;
only the sound of voices is heard.
The returning sunlight enters the deep woods
and shines once more upon the green moss.

Is returning sunlight weird? It conveys late rays/reflected. "Slanting sunlight" common translation of 返景, but literal "returning light" poetic. Could "The last sunlight slants into the deep woods" adds last/slants unsupported somewhat. "Returning light enters the deep forest" accurate and literary. The phrase 返景 means sunlight reflected back? In classical, 返景 = 返照的阳光, setting sun's reflected light. "The sun's returning rays enter the deep wood" plausible.

Perhaps preserve no human visible but voices audible. Four lines. Could do title only plus lines. User didn't request author translated. I can include "Wang Wei" but return only translation maybe title and poem, not author. Typical response expected:
Deer Enclosure

Empty hills, no one in sight,
Only the sound of someone talking;
Late sunlight enters the deep wood,
Shining over the green moss again.
But "someone talking" is good. I want literary.

"The empty mountain holds no one in sight" awkward and adds holds. "No one is seen on the empty mountain;" complete.
"only the echo of voices is heard." 响 not necessarily echo, but resonant sound. "only the sound of voices carries." This uses active carry and avoids repeated heard. Original 但闻 = only hear. Could "I hear only the sound of voices" introduces I implicit but natural. Better no I:
"No one is seen in the empty mountains;
only the sound of voices is heard."
Singular mountain.

"Returning sunlight enters the deep forest,
shining once more upon the green moss." Second relation participle fine, but original repeats shines. Use "and shines again on the green moss."

No need period? Fine.

Respond only.
